questions.q: What is the throughline connecting this course's three chapters?
options: Structure (Chapter 1), motion (Chapter 2), and survival (Chapter 3) — each building directly on the problem the one before it introduced
Chapter order was arbitrary and could be studied in any sequence
Each chapter covers a completely unrelated Fabric feature with no connection to the others
All three chapters cover the exact same material at increasing difficulty
questions.explain: Chapter 3 exists specifically to keep Chapters 1-2's correct pipelines correct once real people, schedules, and failures are involved.

questions.q: What did Chapter 2 demonstrate about Fabric's real-time tools versus Databricks Structured Streaming?
options: The same underlying streaming problems get solved by both, under different labels — different engine, identical computer science
Structured Streaming is strictly superior and Fabric's tools are obsolete
There's no meaningful relationship between the two platforms
Fabric's real-time tools solve a completely different set of problems than Structured Streaming
questions.explain: This comparison (Lesson 40) was a deliberate part of the course's design, not a tangent.

questions.q: Why does Chapter 3's production material matter even for a pipeline Chapters 1-2 already proved works correctly?
options: Chapters 1-2's pipelines are actually already production-ready without any further work
Chapter 3's material is purely optional polish with no real necessity
Production concerns only matter for batch pipelines, not real-time ones
A pipeline that works correctly once, while being watched, is a different bar than one that keeps working correctly unattended, for months, under real failure conditions
questions.explain: This is exactly Lesson 43's opening distinction, revisited here as the reason the whole chapter existed.

questions.q: Where does this course sit in the larger 4-course Data Engineering track?
options: 1st — the very first course in the entire track
It's a standalone course with no connection to any track
3rd — after Data Engineering Foundations and Azure Databricks & Delta Lake, before Data Engineering Career & Capstone
4th and final course in the track, with nothing following it
questions.explain: Every cross-reference back to Databricks & Delta Lake throughout this course exists because the track was designed as one continuous story.

questions.q: Why did this course cross-reference Databricks & Delta Lake so consistently throughout all three chapters?
options: Cross-referencing was only used in Chapter 1, not Chapters 2 or 3
Databricks & Delta Lake content was mistakenly duplicated in this course
The track was designed as one continuous story, not four disconnected courses, so Fabric's concepts were deliberately mapped back to their Databricks equivalents
It was purely coincidental with no deliberate design intent
questions.explain: This deliberate density of cross-referencing was called out from this course's very first lesson.
